chapters.name: Management of Food Safety Practices
chapters.summary: The manager's role in food safety: the person in charge, active managerial control of the CDC risk factors, HACCP, variances, high-risk groups, consumer advisories, staff training, and handling illness complaints.
keyPoints: A person in charge must be present during all hours of operation.
HACCP has seven principles, starting with a hazard analysis.
Special processes such as curing or smoking to preserve food need a variance.

chapters.name: Hygiene and Health
chapters.summary: How food handlers keep food safe: handwashing, glove use, bare-hand contact rules, work clothes and jewelry, wounds, and which symptoms and illnesses mean a worker must be restricted, excluded, or reported.
keyPoints: Handwashing takes at least 20 seconds, with 10 to 15 seconds of scrubbing.
Exclude food handlers with vomiting, diarrhea, or jaundice.
Norovirus, Hepatitis A, Shigella, Shiga toxin-producing E. coli, and Salmonella must be reported.

chapters.name: Safe Receipt, Storage, Transportation and Disposal of Food
chapters.summary: Buying from approved sources, checking deliveries, receiving temperatures, rejecting unsafe food, labeling and date marking, FIFO, refrigerator storage order, chemicals, and recalls.
keyPoints: Receive cold TCS food at 41°F or lower and hot TCS food at 135°F or higher.
Ready-to-eat TCS food can be held 7 days at 41°F; the prep day is day 1.
Store raw food by cooking temperature, with poultry on the bottom shelf.

chapters.name: Safe Preparation and Cooking of Food
chapters.summary: Keeping food out of the temperature danger zone during prep: thawing, minimum internal cooking temperatures, cooling, reheating, time as a public health control, thermometers, cross-contamination, and allergens.
keyPoints: The temperature danger zone is 41°F to 135°F.
Poultry 165°F, ground meat 155°F, seafood and steaks 145°F.
Cool from 135°F to 70°F in 2 hours, then to 41°F in the next 4 hours.

chapters.name: Safe Service and Display of Food
chapters.summary: Holding food for service, checking temperatures, serving and re-serving rules, self-service areas, ice, off-site service, and vending.
keyPoints: Hold hot TCS food at 135°F or higher and cold TCS food at 41°F or lower.
Check held food temperatures at least every 4 hours.
Guests must take a clean plate each time they return to a buffet.

chapters.name: Cleanliness and Sanitation
chapters.summary: Cleaning and sanitizing food-contact surfaces, three-compartment sinks, dishwashers, sanitizer strength, wiping cloths, chemical safety, vomit cleanup, and integrated pest management.
keyPoints: Scrape, wash, rinse, sanitize, and air-dry.
Clean and sanitize surfaces in constant use at least every 4 hours.
Work with a licensed pest control operator as part of integrated pest management.

chapters.name: Facilities and Equipment
chapters.summary: Handwashing stations, approved water, backflow and cross-connections, equipment materials and installation, lighting, garbage, and imminent health hazards such as sewage backups and loss of water or power.
keyPoints: An air gap is the only completely reliable way to prevent backflow.
Floor equipment must be on 6-inch legs or sealed to the floor.
A sewage backup or loss of water service is an imminent health hazard.
